incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) of Hong Kong, sections 67 to 120 (incorporation of companies limited by shares), sections 474 to 482 (company formation documents), and section 113 (share certificates); Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) sections 5 and 6; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) for account and escrow obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong, 14/F, Queensway Government Offices, 66 Queensway, Hong Kong; e-Registry one-stop portal operated jointly with the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Form (Company Limited by Shares) NNC1 together with the Articles of Association filed through the One-Stop Company Formation and Business Registration arrangement.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) does not impose any minimum paid-up share capital, and there is no mandatory escrow or blocked account requirement at incorporation. The company may allot shares at par or premium as resolved by the board. However, for client monies received in study-abroad and visa advisory work, escrow or segregated client accounts are required under banking AML/KYC rules and the Immigration Consultants Codes of Practice where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [CN HK JV LIMITED] (Company No. [______]) ADOPTED IN WRITING ON [DATE]. RESOLVED, as follows: 1. Share Capital and Subscription. That the authorised share capital of the Company be [______] Hong Kong dollars divided into [______] ordinary shares of HK$[______] each, and that the terms of subscription proposed by each subscriber be and are hereby approved. The directors be and are hereby authorised to allot and issue shares, to receive payment by bank transfer or wire payment, and to credit any excess consideration to the share premium account. 2. Banking and Treasury Mandate. That the Company shall open and maintain banking, treasury and escrow accounts at [bank name] or any other licensed bank in Hong Kong as selected by the directors. The directors named in Schedule A be and are hereby appointed as authorised signatories with full authority to execute cheques, wire transfers, foreign exchange transactions, letters of credit, guarantees, escrow arrangements and client money instructions. Any two signatories shall be required for all transactions exceeding HK$[______], and any one signatory shall be sufficient for amounts below that threshold. 3. Registered Office Adoption. That the registered office of the Company be and is hereby established at [physical address within Hong Kong], and that the company secretary be instructed to file the notice of registered office and all particulars with the Companies Registry and to display the statutory name plate at the registered office. 4. Statutory Officers and Consents. That [full name] be appointed as director, [full name] be appointed as company secretary, and [full name] be appointed as statutory auditor. Each officer accepts office upon the terms of the Companies Ordinance, and the company secretary shall maintain the register of members, directors, secretaries, charges and minutes and shall file annual returns and all changes of officer particulars. 5. Corporate Governance and Delegations. That the directors be and are hereby authorised to adopt articles, a common seal, electronic signature infrastructure, bank mandates, AML/KYC procedures, data protection policies, operational risk controls and client money reconciliation rules, and to ratify all pre-incorporation contracts and expenses incurred for the formation of the Company. 6. Force and Certification. This resolution shall take effect immediately and may be executed in counterparts. The chairman and company secretary are jointly and severally authorised to certify, register and file all documents required by law. Certified as a true and complete copy of the first board resolution. Chairman / Company Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Clearance and Articles of Association Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong - e-Registry Portal and Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a company name pre-search through ICRIS to ensure the proposed English name 'CN HK JV LIMITED' and any Chinese name are not identical or too similar to an existing registered name and do not contravene the Companies Ordinance. If available, finalise the Articles of Association, which must be signed by each subscriber in the prescribed form. Verify that all directors, shareholders and the company secretary have provided valid identity documents, address proof and consent to act. Prepare the name-check acknowledgement and retain the filing reference. Pay the small prescribed name-search fee and ensure the return receipt is preserved for the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed company English name and optional Chinese name
Executed Articles of Association signed by all subscribers
Subscriber identity documents and address proof
Consent to act forms for first directors and company secretary
ICRIS name check acknowledgement and fee payment reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as misleading or similar to an existing company, select a new distinctive name, pay the revised search and filing fee, and resubmit through ICRIS; the prior name-check fee is not refundable but may be set against the new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation via One-Stop e-Registry Submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong in coordination with the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and sign Incorporation Form NNC1 (Company Limited by Shares), stating the registered office address, particulars of every first director and the company secretary, and the intended number and amount of issued shares. Attach the signed Articles of Association and any consents included in the NNC1. Submit the full package through e-Registry. The system automatically forwards the application to the Business Registration Office under the one-stop arrangement. Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the Inland Revenue Department issues the Business Registration Certificate. Download, seal and retain both certificates in the statutory records.
required_dossiers: Signed Form NNC1
Signed Articles of Association
Registered office address proof or tenancy/ownership document
Photographic identity and residential address of each proposed director and secretary
Declaration as to compliance with Business Registration Ordinance
Prescribed incorporation fee payment reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried by the Companies Registry, respond in writing within seven working days via e-Registry, explain or correct the discrepancy, re-submit any incorrectly executed signature page, and pay the additional admin fee; if the registry refuses, appeal in writing to the Registrar within twenty-one days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Books, Share Allotment and Share Return
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong and the Company Secretary (or registered service agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the first allotment of shares, prepare and file the Share Return in Form NSC1 to the Companies Registry. Allot shares strictly in accordance with the board resolution on share subscription, issue physical or electronic share certificates and update the register of members. Ensure that the statutory registers of directors, secretaries, charges and minutes are created and maintained at the registered office. Record share premium in the books. Confirm that the Certificate of Incorporation number and company number are stated on share certificates and external documents. If any officer accepts office after incorporation, file the relevant consent form and particulars within the statutory period.
required_dossiers: Board resolution authorising share allotment
Share application and subscription letters from each subscriber
Share certificates issued to all members
Register of members and share premium ledger
Form NSC1 (Share Return)
Consent to act forms for post-incorporation appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry rejects Form NSC1, refile with corrected share count, date, stamp duty declaration and payment receipt within fourteen days; late filing may be remedied by a prescribed late-filing fee and a signed explanation of non-deliberate default.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalisation of Business Registration Certificate and Inland Revenue Notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the initial Business Registration Certificate issued with the Certificate of Incorporation, verify the legal entity name, company number, relevant date of commencement and the prescribed business description. Display the certificate at the registered office and at every physical place of business. If any change of business name, address or scope occurs, file the prescribed notice to the Business Registration Office within fifteen days. Update letterheads, website and client documents with the company number and registered office address. Register the company for employer and tax administrative obligations if staff are engaged. This stage is required before the company can lawfully issue invoices or carry on immigration-visa consulting business.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by Companies Registry
Initial Business Registration Certificate and IRD demand note
Form IRBR1 or notice of change already integrated
Company number and name proof
Registered office operational letterhead template
Authorisation letter of company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Certificate is delayed or contains incorrect classification, attend the Business Registration Office with the incorporation reference number, submit a letter of correction, and request a revised certificate; any late-filing penalty may be mitigated by demonstrating that the one-stop filing was completed on time.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank and Escrow Account Opening with AML/ATF KYC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed banks authorised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA); compliance under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present a certified copy of the first board resolution and the formation dossier to the chosen licensed bank. The resolution must clearly designate authorised signatories, signing thresholds, account utility, permitted payment rails and the segregation of client escrow funds from operating funds. Within the account mandate, permit wire transfers into escrow and then onward transfer only upon completion of admission agreements and satisfactory identification of beneficiaries. Complete the bank's corporate KYC questionnaire, beneficial ownership declaration, source of wealth and source of funds form, and a business narrative explaining the ISIC 7810 migration-visa advisory business. Attend an in-person or video interview as required by the bank.
required_dossiers: Certified Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate
Certified Articles of Association
Certified board resolution for account opening and signatories
Passports and residential addresses of directors and beneficial owners
Completed HKMA-compliant KYC and beneficial ownership declarations
Business plan and projected transaction profile for immigration-visa fees
Escrow or client money account operating procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further evidence, provide source-of-wealth records, agency agreements, liability insurance and audited or pro-forma financial statements within fourteen days; if the application is declined, engage an AML-compliant professional introducer and approach a second licensed bank, preserving all application records for audit trail continuity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 7810 is a pure professional consulting and immigration-visa advisory service; no industrial licensing board, manufacturing authority or physical plant regulator applies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable for industrial or manufacturing operations. The applicable statutory operating authorisation is the Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), together with any professional practice registration required for immigration consultants in destination countries.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no environmental impact assessment, industrial discharge permit, or emissions licensing is triggered for a non-manufacturing consulting operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the activity is classified as office-based professional services with no construction, chemical, assembly, warehousing or manufacturing processes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero process wastewater, zero VOC emissions, zero hazardous waste, and no industrial waste stream; general office waste management and electrical equipment disposal rules under Hong Kong environmental laws apply as ordinary administrative obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial or civil-defense fire-process licensing. As a commercial office, the company must comply with the Fire Safety (Commercial Premises) Ordinance (Cap. 502) by maintaining adequate fire escapes and services inspection approval for the registered office, and with the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) for the safety of employees operating at workstations and the physical premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) and its national unified Electronic Tax Bureau (ETAX) internet portal at etax.chinatax.gov.cn; provincial and municipal STA offices administer registration and audits. The Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department remains the separate competent tax authority for the Hong Kong SAR shareholder for profits tax and income matters in Hong Kong.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The Administration for Market Regulation issues the business license for the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture and generates the Unified Social Credit Code, which constitutes the taxpayer identification number for enterprise income tax and VAT. Step 2: The market regulator transmits the establishment record to the STA Electronic Tax Bureau; the JV must complete supplementary tax registration, including real-name authentication of the legal representative and financial officer, within 30 days of establishment. Step 3: The JV determines its VAT taxpayer identity as a general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer and obtains digital electronic invoice allocation through the Electronic Tax Bureau. Step 4: A foreign non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment that derives China-source income must separately complete non-resident tax registration through its withholding agent at the competent STA office and is assigned a non-resident taxpayer code distinct from the JV Unified Social Credit Code. Step 5: The JV opens a PRC bank account, reports the account to the STA, and registers in the State Administration of Foreign Exchange system for export proceeds collection or cross-border service fee receipt if it will export goods or services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is a PRC resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income at the statutory 25% enterprise income tax rate unless a reduced rate applies. The Hong Kong shareholder is a non-resident enterprise for PRC tax purposes, taxed only on China-source income and potentially eligible for relief under the Mainland and Hong Kong tax arrangement. The study abroad and immigration visa advisory activity is a VAT-taxable consulting service in the PRC at the applicable 6% service VAT rate, with entity-level taxation rather than pass-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; the PRC does not operate a check-the-box or elective entity classification regime equivalent to the United States, and hybrid mismatch outcomes are addressed through the special tax adjustment and general anti-avoidance rules rather than by taxpayer election. The JV may, however, apply for advance pricing arrangements or adopt enterprise income tax preferences only to the extent expressly provided by statute and approved by the STA.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) on the Chinese mainland; Hong Kong SAR has no VAT or GST, and therefore no Hong Kong export VAT zero-rating mechanism.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration applies to all PRC-registered businesses; the mandatory general VAT taxpayer threshold is annual taxable turnover exceeding RMB 5,000,000. Below that threshold the JV may remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer at the simplified 3% collection rate, with temporary legislative reductions where applicable, but a small-scale taxpayer cannot claim input VAT credits or export VAT rebates. The JV should register as a general taxpayer to claim effective 0% export zero-rating and cross-border service refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a nationwide fully digitalized electronic invoice mandate under the Golden Tax Phase IV anti-fraud architecture. Newly registered taxpayers issue invoices through the STA National Electronic Invoice Service Platform inside the Electronic Tax Bureau; each invoice carries a unique digital invoice number and tax-control code, with structured data transmitted in real time to the STA. B2B transactions above platform thresholds require buyer acceptance confirmation, and the platform exposes open API interfaces for ERP integration, red-flush reversals, and reconciliation with customs and foreign-exchange data. Physical pre-printed invoices are not accepted for general VAT taxpayers, and the risk-control engine automatically flags mismatched customs declarations, missing foreign-exchange records, or abnormal zero-rating claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under PRC VAT is available for goods that are declared to Chinese customs, physically exported from the Chinese customs territory, and supported by bank-collected export proceeds in accordance with State Administration of Foreign Exchange regulations. For services, only specifically listed cross-border taxable services such as international transportation, offshore research and development, software, information technology, and design services consumed wholly outside the PRC qualify for the 0% rate. A study abroad and immigration visa advisory service normally qualifies for the cross-border VAT exemption, or for 0% where it is bundled in an approved offshore digital service package, provided the recipient is a non-resident, the service is not performed for PRC domestic consumers, and payment is received through permissible escrow or wire-transfer rails in foreign exchange.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: China Customs Export Goods Declaration (electronic customs export declaration with customs export number)
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing physical exit of the goods from the PRC customs territory
Export sales invoice and the procurement VAT special invoice chain substantiating input tax for export rebate computation

Bank-issued export proceeds collection and remittance verification record in the State Administration of Foreign Exchange system, being the PRC functional equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate
Signed export contract or cross-border service agreement, plus electronic service consumption evidence such as IP address, user location, and delivery records for qualifying offshore digital services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unverified export zero-rating claims are prosecuted as export tax refund fraud. The STA and customs audit the full documentary chain; where supporting documents are missing, inconsistent, or forged, the claimed VAT rebate or zero-rate exemption is retroactively clawed back with statutory late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day from the due date, plus an administrative penalty of 50% to five times the amount of tax involved, and potential disqualification from simplified export refund formalities. Criminal referral may follow under the PRC Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax refunds and false issuance of VAT special invoices, exposing responsible individuals to imprisonment and fines. Retrospective clawback extends up to ten years in fraud cases and up to five years in ordinary tax audits, in addition to the costs of foreign-exchange compliance audits and tax investigation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, acting under the People's Bank of China (PBOC), with associated regulatory coordination through the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) for cross-border clearing channels into the Hong Kong SAR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The PRC operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with full convertibility on the current account for bona fide trade, service, and remittance transactions, while the capital account remains controlled. For a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, the forex administration framework requires SAFE registration of the foreign-invested enterprise, use of a designated onshore foreign currency/capital account, and a genuine, documentation-backed transaction for every FX conversion. Profit remittance by the Hong Kong/foreign shareholder is permissible after annual audit and tax filing, but it is administratively blocked if the tax clearance certificate, audited financial statements, board resolution regarding dividend distribution, and the SAFE remittance purpose code are not complete. Export proceeds are no longer forcibly surrendered to the central bank; however, there is a statutory duty to repatriate overseas receipts and to go through bank collection verification. Any attempt to layer offshore HK treasury vehicles while ignoring the onshore SAFE account and tax documentation will legally fail. Capital inflows for equity subscription also require a capital verification report issued by a licensed PRC certified public accountant. Thus, the convertibility at current account level is strong but conditional; capital account actions such as equity injection, borrowing, and dividends are highly workflow-driven and require dual filing with SAFE and the market supervision authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The current PRC rules do not impose a mandatory conversion ratio into RMB. However, 100% of export foreign currency receipts from cross-border trade and service activities are subject to repatriation into a licensed domestic bank, with the exporter obliged to complete the bank's export-conduct verification within 180 days of customs declaration for goods exports; service export proceeds must be repatriated no later than the contractually agreed payment due date and recorded in the SAFE monitoring system. Retention in a foreign currency account is permitted for bona fide operational needs, but invoices, transport/logistics records, service contracts, and customs declarations must be retained as the bank-level audit trail.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI) plus RMB Basic Operational Currency Account
Cross-Border CNY/FCY Operational Account and SAFE-designated Capital Account
Basic Deposit Account, General Operating Account, and Foreign Exchange Capital Account
Onshore RMB Operational Account and Export Proceeds Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech electronic money institutions are legally and operationally barred from providing the core treasury banking services required by an onshore PRC Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture. A digital EMI from Singapore, the UK, or the EU does not hold a PRC commercial banking licence, cannot open an RMB basic deposit account, cannot appear in SAFE's cross-border foreign exchange reporting system, and cannot issue credible SWIFT MT103 covers or FX settlement reports for capital verification. The feasibility rating is therefore nil or low for any onshore capital inflow, profit remittance, export collection, or tax-related clearing. Such EMIs may at best serve ancillary Hong Kong-side travel cards or expense accounts for overseas principals, but they must never receive the JV's statutory capital or operate as the entity's payment clearing utility in mainland China.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative and the authorised bank signatories of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture must normally appear physically in-branch at the chosen PRC Tier-1 commercial bank, bringing the original business licence, official seals, board resolutions, and identity documents. The bank will also conduct an on-site inspection of the registered operating address and interview the responsible manager under anti-money laundering requirements. Remote consular proxy opening is not a generally accepted substitute for the first account opening; it is permitted only in narrow cases where the legal representative is outside the PRC and executes a notarised power of attorney, and the bank still requires a verification step through a Chinese embassy consular certification or an HKMA-licensed bank's introduced verification, followed by the in-person or encrypted video interview mandated by the individual bank's risk committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity through a Hong Kong shareholder chain and lack of a clean ownership map to the ultimate natural persons controlling the study abroad/immigration advisory firm.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group ownership chart up to the final natural person beneficial owners; Hong Kong Companies Registry certificate of incorporation, annual return, and registered agent certificate of incumbency; notarised board resolutions for the JV and the Hong Kong parent; consent letters of directors; entity risk assessment; and a sworn declaration that no nominee or bearer shares exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial plausibility of immigration-related cross-border fee flows to universities, visa authorities, and overseas golden visa agencies, with risk of disguised client money movement or unlicensed immigration brokering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client contracts with tuition escrow terms; destination-country immigration agency licences and regulatory registration; itemised invoices matching the claimed fees; university offer letters/visa filing receipts; beneficiary account KYC confirmation; and a certified audit trail from the JV operating ledger to the underlying immigration case file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source of funds and source of wealth for the initial equity capital injection and for large operational payments, especially if foreign shareholder funding is sourced from personal savings, family conduits, or offshore family trusts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of personal and corporate bank statements for the funding shareholder; certification of salaries, dividends, and trust distributions; tax returns and tax paid certificates; independent asset verification report by a licensed accountant; source-of-wealth questionnaire; anti-corruption/sanctions screening of all funding counterparties; and the SAFE FDI capital verification report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person and reputational risk exposure because foreign residence or golden visa advisory may attract senior PRC officials, state-owned enterprise executives, or heads of state-owned entities seeking offshore residence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP and adverse media screening snapshot; client KYC declaration confirming no bribery, proceeds of crime, or illegal outward remittance; enhanced due diligence file including independent source-of-funds evidence; no-obligation legal opinion on the immigration programme; compliance committee approval memorandum; and a transaction monitoring escalation plan.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from the Hong Kong shareholder must be wired to the EJV's onshore SAFE-registered capital account using the correct foreign exchange purpose code for a direct foreign investment capital injection, with the remittance narrative identifying the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture name and the equity subscription. The receiving Tier-1 PRC bank will complete SAFE authenticity checks against the FDI basic registration, the approved capital account payment form, the joint venture contract, and the business licence. Each inbound SWIFT MT103/MT202 credit must be matched to the capital verification process, and a licensed PRC certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report before the shareholder is credited with its equity ratio. The bank will then allow conversion into RMB for lawful operating expenses or retention in USD/HKD as the entity's cash position permits, but no early distribution or dividend remittance can occur without annual audit and tax settlement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for tuition fees, student welfare deposits, immigration lawyer retainers, visa application fees, and destination-government golden visa costs should be settled through SWIFT MT103 for foreign currency or through CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) for cross-border RMB, accompanied by the service-trade purpose code and the full supporting dossier known to the paying bank. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are not appropriate for advisory and education expenses; at most, a standby letter of credit can back a performance bond or an escrow arrangement with a regulated destination-country institution. The entity must ensure that every outbound beneficiary account is pre-reviewed and that no high-risk jurisdiction or sanctioned party is in the chain, in line with the Enhanced Due Diligence profile required under its medium-risk AML classification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY forward contracts (USD/CNY, HKD/CNY, and EUR/CNY) executed with a licensed PRC bank after demonstrating genuine FX exposure through underlying operating or tuition payment flows
Short-term FX swaps for converting HKD or USD liquidity into RMB to meet payroll, rent, and immediate service disbursements, subject to SAFE risk-neutral or genuine-backing verification
Cross-currency swaps permitted only for long-term foreign-currency borrowing/equity-related liabilities with SAFE registration and filed underlying financing/loan documentation

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible as a direct hedging tool for the onshore EJV; they may be transacted only by an offshore Hong Kong group treasury vehicle under HKMA-recognised derivatives rules and with no onshore book entry or capital implications

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 42 calendar days after the company's incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If filed late, the higher fee schedule applies: HKD 870 if delivered not more than 3 months after the anniversary, HKD 1,740 if more than 3 but not more than 6 months, HKD 2,610 if more than 6 but not more than 9 months, and HKD 3,480 if more than 9 months. Continued default may result in prosecution and the Registrar may take steps to strike the company off the register, with consequent loss of the limited liability protection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the expiry of the current business registration certificate, which follows the anniversary of commencement of business.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal renders the company and responsible officers liable on summary conviction to a fine of up to HKD 5,000, plus recovery of the unpaid business registration fee and levy. Continued non-compliance can lead to cancellation of the Business Registration Certificate and enforcement action by the Inland Revenue Department.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) with Audited Financial Statements and Tax Computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of the date of issue of the tax return; if a tax representative is appointed, normal extension practice generally grants filing extensions based on the accounting year-end, often to up to 5-8 months after the year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under sections 80 and 82A of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, late filing or failure to file is punishable by a fine of up to HKD 10,000; additional tax of 10% of the tax undercharged may be imposed without prosecution, rising to 15% on conviction. The IRD may issue an estimated assessment and pursue distraint or other recovery proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (Form BIR56A and BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 1 month after the IRD issues the return, normally in April; for most employers the latest due date is 2 May in the year of issue.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file employer returns without reasonable excuse may result in a fine of up to HKD 10,000 under section 80 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, and the Department may require the return to be submitted within a specified notice period. Penalties and added tax may be assessed where tax has been undercharged due to incomplete or inaccurate returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and Laying of Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders/members of the company; minutes and records kept at the registered office and made available for inspection; no filing with Companies Registry for private companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be presented to members no later than 9 months after the end of the accounting reference period; the annual general meeting, if not dispensed with by unanimous written resolution, must be held within the same 9-month window.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible officers may be prosecuted and fined at Level 4 of the Companies Ordinance pecuniary scale (HKD 25,000) with a continuing daily default fine; non-presentation of accounts may also invalidate reliance on the audit exemption for dormant status and increase exposure to tax penalty proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Significant Controllers Register (SCR) annual content confirmation and update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained at the company's registered office; inspection only by law enforcement and authorised officers, not filed with the Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing, with updates required within 7 days of any change to significant controller details; no separate annual filing is made, but the annual return must be consistent with the register as at the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Each responsible officer is liable on conviction to a fine at Level 4 (HKD 25,000) and a further daily default fine of HKD 700 for each day the failure continues if the register is not properly maintained or made available.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount threshold exemptions apply. Under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), every private limited company other than a validly dormant company must appoint a certified public accountant and deliver an independent statutory audit report. Because this study-abroad/immigration-visa consultancy is active and handles client funds through escrow and wire transfers, it cannot claim dormancy and is unconditionally subject to a mandatory annual audit by a CPA.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must comply with Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants; eligible private entities may elect to apply HKFRS for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE) or the Small and Medium-sized Entity Financial Reporting Standard (SME-FRS), provided the entity meets the size tests and disclosure conditions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not operate an annual UBO filing system. Instead, the company must keep a Significant Controllers Register recording any individual or legal entity owning more than 25% of the shares, controlling voting rights, or exercising significant influence. Any change or knowledge of a change must be recorded within 7 days of occurrence. Annual Return NAR1, filed each anniversary, declares the then-current shareholders and directors; this constitutes the annual confirmation to the Registrar. Transfers of shares must be noted in the Register of Members immediately, and the new shareholding thereafter reflected in the next annual return.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.25% on first HKD 2,000,000 of assessable profit; 16.5% on profit above HKD 2,000,000 (two-tiered profits tax for corporations)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Hong Kong levies no capital gains tax, no dividend tax, no VAT/GST, and no withholding tax on dividends; available incentives include two-tiered rates, full depreciation allowances (initial annual allowance, annual allowance for industrial buildings), deductions for R&D under IRO s.16E, tax exemption for certain offshore funds, and no tax on foreign-source income under the territorial principle

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profits Tax Return - Corporation (Form BIR51) filed via the Inland Revenue Department eTAX electronic filing portal (https://www.etax.gov.hk)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due within 1 month of the issue date. For accounting periods ending 31 December, the BIR51 is generally issued on the first working day of April and the eTAX filing deadline may be extended to 15 November; for periods ending 31 March, the return is issued in August and may be extended to 15 November; any extension requires timely lodgment of the Employer Return and provisional tax at the prescribed schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the company name, legal form (Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture), Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate number, and registered office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the exact legal name in English and the Business Registration (BR) number. If the JV is a Hong Kong-registered company with mainland Chinese ultimate beneficial owners, mark clearly that the entity is resident in Hong Kong for tax treaty purposes and specify the place of effective management. Any inconsistency with the BR certificate will trigger an IRD objection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the accounting period covered by the return, e.g. 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a newly incorporated JV, the first basis period may be longer than 12 months. All profits arising in or derived from Hong Kong must be declared for that period. If the JV has a foreign-controlled board making decisions offshore, the IRD will scrutinise the place of key management and commercial control to determine territorial source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3/Nature of Business Principal Economic Activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use the Hong Kong Standard Industrial Classification (HSIC) code corresponding to ISIC 7810 / NAICS 541199 - International Student Placement and Golden Visa Residence Advisory. Provide a narrative in the 'Business activities' field.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a cross-border study-abroad and immigration consultancy, describe the two core streams: (i) overseas student placement services and (ii) immigration/visa advisory services. Clearly indicate where each service is performed (Hong Kong, mainland China, or overseas). If the JV earns commissions from overseas educational institutions for introducing students, such commission income is typically assessable in Hong Kong if the negotiation and conclusion of the contract occur in Hong Kong; if contracts are concluded outside Hong Kong, the territorial source must be demonstrated with full supporting evidence (contracts, emails, board minutes, location of employees).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the audited net profit after taxation per the Hong Kong financial statements prepared under Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The audited accounts must include full disclosure of all revenue, including fees paid by students for visa processing, university application assistance, and residence-by-investment programmes. The non-resident JV must not reduce this figure by foreign income that is allegedly offshore unless a valid offshore claim is made; the burden of proving non-source lies entirely on the taxpayer under IRO s.14. If the company claims a portion of service fees as not assessable, provide a precise time-based and activity-based apportionment, not a fixed percentage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5/Add Back Items Adj        ustments to Accounting Profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back disallowable expenses: depreciation not allowed, donations not made, taxes paid to mainland China not recoverable, private expenses, penalties, fines, and any provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Chinese-HK JV, common add-backs include group management fees, brand royalties, and reimbursement of mainland employees' social security contributions. These deductions are allowed only if wholly and exclusively incurred in the production of assessable profits. Under IRO s.16(1) and the Hong Kong transfer pricing rules, any intercompany charge must be arm's length; an add-back will be required if the IRD challenges either the commercial substance or the deduction amount. Do not deduct Shanghai/Beijing corporate income tax paid by the Chinese parent, as it is not a Hong Kong tax and is only creditable in mainland China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6/Deduct: Non-Assessable Income and Exempt Profits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct income not subject to Hong Kong profits tax, including foreign-source dividends (with exceptions), capital gains, and income from a trade carried on outside Hong Kong.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the most dangerous box for a treaty-driven JV. Merely registering a Hong Kong company and concluding contracts offshore does not establish non-source. The IRD will examine where the CIGA - client solicitation, contract negotiation, exam evaluation, visa submission, and fee collection - physically occur. If the JV's employees in Hong Kong admit mainland students, sign on behalf of the university, or email the visa application, the entire commission is taxable in Hong Kong. If the JV is a conduit billing company with no staff, the IRD will ignore the offshore claim and treat the income as fully assessable, plus impose penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7/Net Assessable Profits (After Loss Relief and Capital Allowances)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the adjusted assessable profit after capital allowances (depreciation) and set-off of prior-year losses. This is the figure on which profits tax at the two-tiered rate is charged.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File the provisional tax computation in the prescribed schedule. For a JV with a mainland parent, any tax loss relief claimed must satisfy the continuity of trade test under IRO s.19C; a change in the shareholding on the mainland side may invalidate the loss carryforward. Capital allowances on equipment used in the immigration visa business (e.g. computer servers, online filing devices) are deductible at 20% per year, but motor cars and foreign property are subject to caps. Ensure that the final assessable profit is rounded to the nearest HKD and declared as such.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file Form BIR51 triggers IRO s.80(2): fine of HKD 10,000 and a further fine of three times the tax undercharged. Under IRO s.82A, willful evasion with intent (e.g. omission of commissions or fabricated deductions) is punishable by a fine of HKD 50,000 plus three times the tax undercharged and imprisonment for 3 years. Upon conviction, a daily default penalty of HKD 300 per day under s.85 can be imposed until the return is filed. The IRD may also issue an estimated assessment based on available information, which must be paid immediately and is not stayed pending objection.
